rules: Multiplying a cross-sectional fundamental rank by a price-normalized range term is what paid: all three accepts above 4.0 had that shape. Every additive fundamental +/- volume-rank combo died on the cheap screen (|t| 0.52 and 0.06).

Volume on its own is weak or duplicative: TS_ARGMAX($volume,21) scored 0.70, the 21d volume CV 1.43, and TS_RANK($volume,21) hit rho 0.94 against the dollar-volume z-score. Volume paid only when correlated against a second series (TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 21) = 4.98).
$return as an input is dead on this fit window: TS_MEAN($return,21) gave |t| 0.35 and TS_CORR($return,$volume,10) gave |t| 0.09. Build the same ideas from price levels and $high-$low instead.

Ratios of two windows of the same series failed the cheap screen every time (volume 5/21 -> 0.66, range 21/5 -> 0.19). Normalize against a different series or a price level, not against a longer window of itself.

Near-copies of archive members caused 11 of 20 rejects: swapping one price leaf ($high for $close), one window constant (10->21, 21->189), inverting a ratio, or wrapping an existing term in TS_MEAN at the same window (rho 0.824). Change an operator or a whole input, not a parameter.

A difference of two fundamental ranks submitted alone tracks its dominant leg (RANK($roa)-RANK($accrual_gap) hit rho 0.802 against RANK($roa)). The same spread cleared at 4.11 once multiplied by a price term, so gate fundamental spreads rather than proposing them bare.
Do not put adjusted $close and raw OHLC in the same ratio or difference; it is a scale error that leaks future dividend information, whatever fitness it reports.

Slot economics: fast/price_volume is held at only 1.43 and slow/price_volume at 0.70, so those are the cheap wins. slow/mixed is now held at 4.76 and 4.11 by fundamental-times-range factors, so further variants of that shape will mostly trip the correlation and subtree gates.
